findings.evidence: Lines 82–85 define `kostantTorusScheme` from arbitrary `b : Basis (Fin n) ℤ M` and `wt : Fin n → κ → ℤ`; lines 89–93 assume only `Submodule.span ℤ (Set.range wt) = ⊤` and conclude `IsClosedImmersion`.
findings.fix: Describe it consistently as the split torus represented diagonally by the supplied weights, and state that identifying it as a maximal/Kostant torus requires additional representation or ambient-group hypotheses.
findings.issue: The module title/prose and declaration docs at lines 77 and 95 call the constructed object the “split maximal torus,” but `kostantTorusScheme` accepts any basis `b` and weight function `wt`; even the spanning hypothesis only proves a closed immersion, not maximality in `GLₙ` or identification with a Chevalley-group torus.

summary: The Torus module repeatedly labels an arbitrary diagonal split torus as “maximal” and “Kostant” without hypotheses establishing either property.
